title: Spex Project Config
description: Project configuration (spex.yaml): the project and the packages that spex manages together.

cli_version.description: Semantic version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) of the spex CLI that wrote this config. spex warns when a command that loads the project finds a mismatch with the installed CLI; run `spex update` to sync.

layout.description: How the project is arranged on disk. `multi-repo`: every package is its own git repository under the project root and the spex repository is the spex directory. `single-repo`: the project is one git repository and the spex directory is its `spex/` folder. `monorepo`: one git repository holds several packages and the spex directory is its `spex/` folder.

agent_root.description: Directory holding the agent files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/skills/`, `.claude`), relative to the spex directory: `.` in multi-repo, `..` (the repository root) in single-repo and monorepo.

description.description: Optional summary of what the project is and does.

rules_unused.description: Rule IDs deliberately removed from this project's `rules/`. `spex update` respects a listed ID by never redeploying its bundled template; any bundled rule missing locally but not listed here is treated as newly available upstream and gets deployed.

packages.description: Packages that spex manages for this project.

package_name.description: Full kebab-case name of the package, `<project-name>-<package-short-name>` (for example `shopping-notes-api`). In multi-repo it matches the package directory name per naming-convention; in single-repo it is the project name.

package_short_name.description: Kebab-case name of the package excluding the project name (for example `api`; in single-repo the project name itself). Used to derive cross-cutting identifiers in naming-convention.

description.description: Optional summary of what the package is and does.

path.description: Path to the package, relative to the spex directory.

contracts.description: Interface contracts this package owns. Each entry points at a contract file wherever it lives (typically inside this package's own directory; the spex repository's `contracts/` folder is only a convention for contracts shared across packages) and summarizes it.

rules.description: Rule IDs that apply to this package. Each ID corresponds to a yaml file named after it under `rules/` (for example `secret-handling` -> `rules/secret-handling.yaml`).

exclude.description: Glob patterns, the same globs a check's `include` and `exclude` use, matched against the path of every file and folder relative to this package's root, naming what `spex check` and `spex coverage` leave out of this package only, merged with the `exclude` of this package's `spex.package.yaml`. A folder that matches is skipped with everything inside it: `vendor` or `**/vendor` skips a folder, `vendor/**` the files inside it, and `**/*.generated.ts` such files at any depth. An excluded file is never checked, and its `@spec` annotations count for no spec; contract files declared in `contracts` are not affected.

check_ignore.description: Baseline of pre-existing `error`-severity findings to suppress for this package only, merged with the `check_ignore` of this package's `spex.package.yaml`, so a check can be enforced going forward without first fixing every existing violation. Each entry names the check by `rule_id` + `check`; an `error` finding from that check is dropped when its location file is listed in `files` (or always, when `files` is omitted or empty). New errors in other files still surface, and `warn`-severity findings are never affected.

coverage_ignore.description: Coverage requirements this package waives for specs, merged with the `coverage_ignore` of this package's `spex.package.yaml`. Each entry is a spec's `coverage_ignore` entry plus the `spec_id` it applies to. A requirement of a spec is waived once every package the spec lists in `packages` waives it, or the spec's own `coverage_ignore` does, so a waiver of one package never affects another package's requirement.

contract.description: An interface contract owned by a package: OpenAPI, proto, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, or, for a UI-facing spec, a design reference — a markdown document linking the spec to its visual design.

path.description: Path to the contract file, relative to the spex directory (for example `../shopping-notes-api/contracts/api.openapi.yaml` when the contract lives in the owning package, or `contracts/api.openapi.yaml` when it lives in the spex repository's shared `contracts/` folder).

description.description: Short summary of what the contract covers (for example `admin rest openapi spec`).

spec_coverage_ignore.description: A coverage waiver for one spec: `layer` (`contract`, `impl`, or `test`) is required; `ac` is optional — omit it to waive that layer for the whole spec, or give an acceptance criterion id to waive just that one criterion's impl or test annotation, or its contract annotation under `contract: for-each-ac`. `spex check` verifies the waiver matches the spec's `contract` setting.

spec_id.description: Spec ID of the spec whose coverage requirement is waived.

ignored_error.description: A baseline entry that suppresses pre-existing `error`-severity findings for one check.

rule_id.description: Rule ID of the check whose pre-existing errors are baselined. Must be one of the package's rules.

check.description: Name of the check whose pre-existing errors are baselined.

files.description: Package-relative files whose pre-existing errors are suppressed. Omit or leave empty to suppress the whole check. A regexp finding's `file:line` location is matched on its file part.

examples.description: Shopping list app for keeping track of items to buy.

packages.description: Backend service that handles shopping items.

contracts.description: REST OpenAPI spec for the shopping items API.

packages.description: React web client that lets users manage their shopping notes.
